stage_2_story.text_en: David had promised his daughter Noa a night she would never forget, and he kept his word. The venue was a grand outdoor amphitheatre on the edge of the city, and the moment they walked through the gates, Noa grabbed his arm with excitement. They stopped at the merchandise stand and she picked out a T-shirt with the band's logo, while David bought a poster to hang in her room. The setlist was taped to a speaker by the stage, and Noa read every song title aloud, counting down to her favourites. The opening act played a quiet acoustic set that silenced the crowd — just two guitars and a single voice floating through the warm night air. Then came the main band after their final rehearsal, and the whole amphitheatre exploded with cheering. Song after song filled the night sky, and when the lights went dark after the last number, nobody moved. The crowd clapped and stomped until the band walked back out for an encore, playing two more songs to thunderous applause. At the very end, every person in the venue rose to their feet and gave a standing ovation that lasted a full minute. David looked at Noa — her face lit up, her voice gone from singing — and he thought to himself that this small gig in their city was better than any world tour he had ever watched on television. On the drive home, she rested her head on his shoulder and said, 'Dad, this was the best night of my life.'
